subject: Renewal proposal & bridge-credit for Orchid AI
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@orchidai.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Chris Bell <chris.bell@orchidai.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal ask + bridge credit question

Hi Elliot —

Thanks again for the renewal draft. Our finance and procurement teams reviewed the numbers and have two quick asks before we can move to internal approval: 1) can you clarify the proposed bridge credit mechanics (how it draws down and any cap), and 2) is Redwood open to a 12-month price hold for 2028 if we commit now?

Attached is our May usage report (orchid_usage_may2027.csv) so you can see the burst pattern — we had two months above our committed baseline. Procurement is nervous about overage exposure mid-year.

High level we like the idea of a 12‑month renewal with a modest uplift to committed units, but they want an explicit mitigation path for bursts (credits / temporary burst pool) rather than punitive overage pricing.

Can you propose 1–2 structured options we can present to our CFO this week? Short call would help — timezone PT works best.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Partnerships
Orchid AI

Attachment: orchid_usage_may2027.csv

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@orchidai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal ask + bridge credit question

Samira —

Appreciate the usage file, that makes the burst pattern clear. Below are two practical options that preserve unit economics for both sides and give you predictable capex treatment for the CFO: 

Option A — 12m renewal (preferred operational simplicity)
- 12 months term, 8% standard renewal discount off list rates
- $200k bridge credit applied as a drawdown against overage charges for the first 6 months; credit draws only when monthly usage > committed baseline
- True-up at month 6 and month 12 (usage vs committed)
- Price hold for base unit rate through 2027 only

Option B — 24m renewal (price stability + deeper discount)
- 24 months, 12% renewal discount
- $120k upfront credit (applied over first 4 months); additional burst buffer configurable
- Formal price-hold clause for calendar year 2028 on base rates
- Quarterly true-ups

Pros/cons: A is lower commitment, larger bridge credit; B gives you longer price predictability and smaller immediate credit. We can tighten the drawdown language so credits are non-refundable and only reduce overage invoices.

Next steps: I can put a short SOW amendment (Redwood_SOW_v2.pdf) on DocuSign for the option you prefer. Happy to jump on a 30‑minute call tomorrow afternoon PT to walk Finance through the mechanics.

- Elliot
Elliot Price
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SOW_v2.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@orchidai.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal ask + bridge credit question

Looping in a small tweak from our side — thanks for the thoughtful options. A couple practical guardrails we typically add so credits don't materially change unit economics: 

- Cap the bridge-credit redemption at 40% of monthly overage to avoid complete bill washouts in a burst month.
- Include a trigger to convert unused portion of the credit to one-time discount if not used by month 6 (helps forecasting).
- If you prefer a full price-hold for 2028, we'd look to a modest escalation on support SLA for the longer commit (nothing significant, just a built-in review clause).

If Orchid's procurement needs a PO in advance of DocuSign, we can accept an intent PO and follow with the SOW amendment. Legal usually asks for simple amendment language documenting credit drawdown and true‑up cadence.

Happy to align on a final option — propose we aim to get a signature by Jun 18 so we can lock capacity for Q3 & Q4.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Lead Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@orchidai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Orchid AI - Legal <legal@orchidai.com>, Chris Bell <chris.bell@orchidai.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal ask + bridge credit question

Thanks Ben — that cap and the convert-to-discount trigger make sense. After a quick budget committee chat, Orchid is prepared to move on Option A with a couple of clarifications: 

1) We want the bridge credit split: $120k upfront applied over the first three months, $80k as a reserve that only kicks in for true burst months (records show two such months in the last 12).
2) Cap the monthly redemption at 50% of overage (procurement pushed back from 40 to 50).
3) Need a clause that any unused reserve transfers to a one-time invoice credit if not used by month 6.
4) Legal wants the amendment language, then we'll issue an intent PO to match the amendment value.

Attaching the PO intent note so you can see internal approvers and timeline (Orchid_PO_intent.txt). We can sign once legal confirms the amendment text.

On timing: target to sign before Jun 25 — can Redwood get SOW v3 and DocuSign by Jun 18?

— Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Partnerships
Orchid AI

Attachment: Orchid_PO_intent.txt

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@orchidai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Orchid AI - Legal <legal@orchidai.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal ask + bridge credit question — SOW and next steps

Samira —

Thanks — appreciate the clarity from procurement. Per your asks above, we've produced an updated amendment and SOW (Redwood_SOW_v3.pdf) that implements Option A with the split credit (120k upfront / 80k reserve), 50% monthly redemption cap, and the unused-reserve conversion at month 6. Legal redline highlights are in the SOW margin notes.

Next steps: 
- I attached SOW_v3 and created a DocuSign packet (https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/abc-orchid-amend) for the amendment and SOW.
- If you confirm, we'll send the DocuSign to Samira and Chris and copy your legal inbox.
- Once signed, we will schedule a QBR + kickoff to align burst-handling and observability (30–45 minutes).

I'll also update the HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567) with the agreed terms and mark the close target as 2027-06-25. Deal ID: RBW-2027-ORCH-14.

If that timeline works, I'll route DocuSign now so legal sees the amendment language.

Best,
Elliot Price
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v3.pdf, Redwood_SOW_v3-redline_notes.txt
